text:
maria: Hey team — syncing on the Ampere perf/W benchmark with NVIDIA. Can we lock a run window next week? I put a short spec here: https://redwood-internal/bench/specs/ampere-perfw.md :point_right:

nvidia-eng: We can do Wed/Thu mornings PT. We'll bring the kernel patches (L0/L1) and driver telemetry. Need confirmation on target batch sizes and target power cap.

cheng: For metrics, let's track tokens/sec, p95 latency, power (W) sampled every 1s, and stability (stddev throughput). Also energy per token = W * time / tokens. Target: >= 1.8 tokens/J for 512 seq on fp16/8-bit quant.

alek: +1 to that metric set. Quick note — our harness needs the CUDA env + a custom kernel param: 
```
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
./bench_harness --model r-instruct-3B --seq 512 --batch 8 --dtype fp16 --profile power --samples 1000
```
We'll forward the exact harness version.

clara: Do we want to run the small/medium/large matrix? i.e., batch [1,4,8,16], seq [128,512,2048]? Might be heavy. I suggest focus on 128 & 512 first.

maria: Agree — start with batch 1/8 and seq 128/512. If those look good, expand. Also want kernel tuning flags list from NVIDIA so we can reproduce.

nvidia-eng: We'll send `nv_tune_v1` flags tomorrow. Also would like to test two power caps: 250W and 300W. That lets us measure perf/W curve.

cheng: Can bench-bot ingest power telemetry? If so, we can auto-plot tokens/sec vs W.

bench-bot: yes — I can parse the CSV output and produce perf/W plots. Format I expect: `ts, watts, tokens, latency_ms`. Attach output to thread when done.

alek: FYI here's a sample run excerpt (sanitized):
```
[RUN] model=r-instruct-3B dtype=fp16 batch=8 seq=512
throughput: 142 tokens/sec
power_avg: 280 W
latency_p95: 210 ms
energy_per_1000_tokens: 1.97 kJ
```
Interpretation: tokens/W = 142 / 280 = 0.507 tokens/sec/W -> energy_per_token ~ 1.97 J (we want tokens/J so invert). We should compute tokens/J consistently.

maria: Good catch on units. We'll standardize to tokens_per_joule = tokens_total / (watts_avg * seconds). Add unit note to spec.

clara: Who's owner for test infra config and artifact upload? I can own artifact uploads to S3. Need someone to own infra scheduling.

maria: @alek you ok to own infra scheduling? Clara will do uploads.

alek: I can do infra scheduling and will provision the test node + toggles for power cap.

nvidia-eng: Also important — kernel tune may change perf shape for small batches. Please run the baseline (no-tune) first, then tuned. We'll label runs accordingly.

bench-bot: Action items logged: 1) baseline runs (maria/alek) 2) tuned runs (nvidia-eng + alek) 3) upload artifacts (clara) 4) ingest & plot (bench-bot). I will post a summary thread with CSV + PNGs after the run window.

cheng: For the report, include per-model breakdown and a short blurb about quantization/accuracy tradeoff (we'll run a small eval). Keep it to 1 pager for partner announcement.

maria: Perfect. Let's confirm run window: Wed 2026-04-01 08:00-12:00 PT. @nvidia-eng does that work?

nvidia-eng: Confirmed. We'll be on call at 07:45 PT to stage.

maria: Great — I'll send calendar invites + brief run checklist. Thanks all :rocket:
